note: Regorafenib and lenvatinib reached HCC patients on a filed syngeneic hepatoma survival model and HCC xenografts; their efficacy results are retrodictions because sorafenib had already shown VEGFR multikinase benefit in HCC, rat/dog/monkey toxicology predicted liver harm that HCC patients showed (mildly for regorafenib), and donafenib and catequentinib have patient data but no model comparison found.
label: HCC (VEGFR multikinase)

engagement.model: Syngeneic orthotopic H129 hepatoma in C3H/HeN mice (survival endpoint)
engagement.note: Bayer's filed HCC model read survival only; no pharmacodynamic marker was measured, so nothing could be compared with dosed patients.
engagement.short: Filed hepatoma model read survival only
engagement.quote: In C3H/HeN mice, H129 hepatoma cells (a syngenic tumor) were implanted into the liver (upper left lobe).
engagement.judgement: The only HCC model in the regorafenib NDA (report A58231) has no PD readout at all; the review reports survival and body weight only. Untested, not blank: a model existed.

engagement.confidence_note: The 2015 review lists the study title only; the readouts come from the published version (Matsuki 2018, abstract-level).
engagement.model: Human HCC cell-line and patient-derived xenografts in immunodeficient mice
engagement.note: Eisai filed a PLC/PRF/5 HCC xenograft; its readouts (tumour microvessel density, FRS2 phosphorylation) were never measured in HCC patients.
engagement.short: Xenograft MVD never measured in patients
engagement.quote: W-20130793 Comparison of Antitumor Effects of E7080 and Sorafenib on PLC/PRF/5 Human Hepatocellular Carcinoma Xenografts in Mice
engagement.reason: Model PD readouts never measured in patients
engagement.judgement: Matsuki 2018 reports MVD and tumour pFRS2/pErk as the PD readouts; REFLECT biomarker work measured serum proteins (VEGF, FGF19/23, ANG2), a different quantity, and no HCC biopsy MVD series exists. Untested rather than a downstream same.

dose.model: Syngeneic orthotopic H129 hepatoma in C3H/HeN mice (survival endpoint)
dose.note: Mice got 10 mg/kg/day; the review states no mouse exposure at that dose against the 160 mg clinical exposure.
dose.short: 10 mg/kg mouse dose, no exposure match
dose.quote: Four or five days after implant, groups of 8 mice were untreated, dosed with vehicle or dosed with 10 mg/kg/day of regorafenib orally until death
dose.judgement: The efficacy section gives the dose but no toxicokinetics; the exposure margins in the review are for toxicology species, not the hepatoma mice.

dose.confidence_note: Review lists the xenograft study title only; no exposure target for the HCC model is stated anywhere I read.
dose.model: Human HCC cell-line and patient-derived xenografts in immunodeficient mice
dose.note: Lenvatinib's HCC dose (12 or 8 mg by body weight) came from HCC phase 1 pharmacokinetics, not from a xenograft exposure target.
dose.short: HCC dose set by patient PK, not model
dose.quote: W-20130793 Comparison of Antitumor Effects of E7080 and Sorafenib on PLC/PRF/5 Human Hepatocellular Carcinoma Xenografts in Mice
dose.judgement: Neither the 2015 review nor Matsuki 2018 (abstract) states the xenograft exposure against the clinical one, so the track stays untested; the sibling track scores the class dose question.

dose.magnitude_basis: mouse plasma exposure at 10 mg/kg versus human exposure at 160 mg/day, stated as matching
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the mouse AUC figures are in the full text, which I did not read.
dose.model: Syngeneic orthotopic H129 hepatoma in C3H/HeN mice (survival endpoint)
dose.note: Bayer states the 10 mg/kg mouse dose recapitulates human exposure at the MTD; RESORCE dosed 160 mg and improved survival. Retrodiction ruling: the exposure match was first public in 2017, after regorafenib's own 160 mg patient results (phase 1, CORRECT, RESORCE), so it is scored retro, not same.
dose.short: Mouse exposure matched 160 mg; drug worked
dose.quote: Both drugs were administered orally once daily at 10 mg/kg (regorafenib) or 30 mg/kg (sorafenib), which recapitulate the human exposure at the maximally tolerated dose in mice.
dose.reason: Effective mouse exposure reached at 160 mg
dose.judgement: Scored same under 'reached, drug worked': the paper puts mouse and human exposure side by side (comparison_stated) and RESORCE succeeded at the matched dose. Published after RESORCE, but the H129 study itself was filed in 2012 (same 27-vs-36-day result), but the dose claim itself (mouse exposure matched to the human 160 mg exposure) was first public in 2017 and is built on regorafenib's own earlier patient exposure, so under the dose retrodiction rule it is retro. No NOAEL-type margin is stated (mice lost about 8% body weight), so margin_stated is false.

dose.note: Eisai's popPK/exposure-response model (healthy-volunteer, solid-tumour and Study 202 HCC data) picked 12 mg (>=60 kg) / 8 mg (<60 kg) for phase 3; no patient test yet.
dose.short: PK model picks weight-based phase 3 dose
dose.quote: We therefore recommend 12-mg and 8-mg starting doses for subjects ≥60 kg and <60 kg, respectively, in subjects with HCC Child-Pugh class A.
dose.confidence_note: Proxy opening: the analysis was published 2017 (epub 2017-05-31) but the regimen it recommends was REFLECT's from its March 2013 start (NCT01761266, bodyweight stratification), so the model existed by 2013. Full text read (PMC5575539). model_filed true on the 2018 HCC label (section 2.4 weight-based dose); the 2018 sNDA review PDFs themselves returned 404.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first use. Model is in silico (logistic exposure-response on cycle-1 dose modifications; AUC cutoff 2430 ng·h/mL, body-weight cutoff 57.8 kg), not an animal.
dose.model: Population PK / exposure-response model of lenvatinib in HCC (phase 1 pool + Study 202) choosing weight-based starting dose

dose.note: REFLECT dosed exactly the model's regimen (12 mg >=60 kg / 8 mg <60 kg) and met its OS non-inferiority primary endpoint: regimen reached and enough. Design: REFLECT tested this regimen in a non-inferiority trial against sorafenib.
dose.short: Model's weight-based dose used; REFLECT worked
dose.quote: to receive oral lenvatinib (12 mg/day for bodyweight ≥60 kg or 8 mg/day for bodyweight <60 kg) or sorafenib 400 mg twice-daily in 28-day cycles.
dose.confidence_note: Paired by me (Tamai 2017 model vs Kudo 2018 trial); REFLECT's observed exposure by weight group is not reported in the abstract, so magnitude is null. Abstract-level reading of Kudo 2018. The 2018 FDA label (206947s007, sections 2.4 and 14.3) carries the same regimen at tier 2 but does not state the comparison.
dose.judgement: Scored same under 'reached, drug worked': the trial gave the model-chosen regimen and OS was non-inferior (HR 0.92). margin_stated true because the model named a tolerated exposure ceiling (AUC 2430 ng·h/mL, early dose modification) and set the regimen below it; patients were dosed to that target and the trial succeeded. Year is the Lancet publication (2018), not the 2017 Tamai paper, since the trial result is the patient side. No regulator review of the 2018 HCC sNDA was retrievable, so comparison_stated stays false.
dose.model: Population PK / exposure-response model of lenvatinib in HCC (phase 1 pool + Study 202) choosing weight-based starting dose

efficacy.model: Syngeneic orthotopic H129 hepatoma in C3H/HeN mice (survival endpoint)
efficacy.note: Regorafenib 10 mg/kg/day prolonged survival of mice with orthotopic H129 hepatoma (half alive at day 35 vs 27); no HCC trial yet.
efficacy.quote: When hepatoma bearing mice were administered regorafenib at a dose level of 10 mg/kg daily, there was increased survival compared to either untreated or vehicle treated controls.
efficacy.judgement: Report A58231 is the one HCC model in the colorectal NDA, filed four years before RESORCE read out. The review's summary calls the host Balb/c while the study section says C3H/HeN; I follow the study section.

efficacy.confidence_note: Result not described in the review (data not shown); the published version is Matsuki 2018.
efficacy.model: Human HCC cell-line and patient-derived xenografts in immunodeficient mice
efficacy.note: Eisai filed a lenvatinib-versus-sorafenib PLC/PRF/5 HCC xenograft in the thyroid NDA; the review gives the title, not the result.
efficacy.short: Lenvatinib vs sorafenib HCC xenograft filed
efficacy.quote: W-20130793 Comparison of Antitumor Effects of E7080 and Sorafenib on PLC/PRF/5 Human Hepatocellular Carcinoma Xenografts in Mice
efficacy.judgement: Listed to date the model before REFLECT (first posted 2013, read out 2017). Product in model, filed, but the prediction itself is only public in 2018.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: relative gain in median survival, mouse vs RESORCE
efficacy.model: Syngeneic orthotopic H129 hepatoma in C3H/HeN mice (survival endpoint)
efficacy.note: RESORCE: regorafenib after sorafenib improved overall survival (HR 0.63; 10.6 vs 7.8 months), as the hepatoma survival model predicted. Retrodiction ruling: efficacy is a claim about the target, and sorafenib, a VEGFR multikinase inhibitor, had already prolonged survival in HCC patients (SHARP, 2007-2008) before this model result was public, so it is scored retro. Design: placebo-controlled, overall survival primary, second line after sorafenib.
efficacy.quote: Regorafenib improved overall survival with a hazard ratio of 0·63 (95% CI 0·50-0·79; one-sided p<0·0001); median survival was 10·6 months (95% CI 9·1-12·1) for regorafenib versus 7·8 months (6·3-8·8) for placebo.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: model side is the 2012 FDA review (tier 2); the trial paper does not cite the mouse study. Dated to the Lancet online date (6 Dec 2016), before the registry posting (June 2017). Magnitude on the relative gain in median survival: mouse +30% (27 to 35 days), patients +36% (7.8 to 10.6 months), within 2x; the mouse model was treatment-naive, patients were sorafenib-progressed.

patient_trials.quote: Regorafenib is the only systemic treatment shown to provide survival benefit in HCC patients progressing on sorafenib treatment.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PLC5 xenograft tumour inhibition at 20-40 mg/kg/d vs RESORCE overall survival benefit
efficacy.note: Tai 2014 showed regorafenib inhibiting PLC5 HCC xenografts before RESORCE read out; RESORCE then improved survival (HR 0.63). Retrodiction ruling: efficacy is a claim about the target, and sorafenib, a VEGFR multikinase inhibitor, had already prolonged survival in HCC patients (SHARP, 2007-2008) before this model result was public, so it is scored retro.
efficacy.quote: Regorafenib improved overall survival with a hazard ratio of 0·63 (95% CI 0·50-0·79; one-sided p<0·0001); median survival was 10·6 months (95% CI 9·1-12·1) for regorafenib versus 7·8 months (6·3-8·8) for placebo.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by me: Tai 2014 (epub 2014-09-23, PMID 25248379; abstract read: 'Regorafenib induced significant tumor inhibition') vs Bruix 2017 (online 2016-12-06, PMID 27932229, abstract read). Academic study, not filed. Xenograft was treatment-naive PLC5, patients sorafenib-progressed. Tai 2014 is the system's first use in the class, so model_first_use_year is 2014.
efficacy.judgement: Prospective regorafenib prediction on the xenograft track: published 2014, before RESORCE (2016), so scored same rather than retro, dated to the Lancet online date. Precedes Kissel 2017 retro on the same track. Dose 20-40 mg/kg/d is 2-4x the exposure-matched 10 mg/kg, a dose-cell matter not scored here.
efficacy.model: Human HCC cell-line and patient-derived xenografts in immunodeficient mice

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour growth inhibition in 8/10 PDX models vs RESORCE survival benefit
efficacy.model: Human HCC cell-line and patient-derived xenografts in immunodeficient mice
efficacy.note: After RESORCE, Bayer ran 10 HCC patient-derived xenografts: regorafenib inhibited 8/10, beating sorafenib in four, offered as explaining the clinic. Second retro on the regorafenib xenograft track (PDX panel), kept as strengthening.
efficacy.short: Post-hoc PDX panel reproduces regorafenib benefit
efficacy.quote: Overall, both regorafenib and sorafenib were effective in mouse models of HCC, although several cases showed better regorafenib activity which may explain the observed efficacy of regorafenib in sorafenib-refractory patients.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: published November 2017, eleven months after RESORCE, and the authors frame the PDX result as explaining the trial. Filed on the xenograft track because the PDX panel is new; the H129 arm repeats the 2012 filed study (36 vs 27 days).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: antitumour activity vs sorafenib in xenografts against OS non-inferiority
efficacy.confidence_note: Model result read at abstract level (Matsuki 2018); the filed 2015 study's numbers are not in the FDA review. Lancet online date taken as February 2018.
efficacy.model: Human HCC cell-line and patient-derived xenografts in immunodeficient mice
efficacy.note: REFLECT: lenvatinib non-inferior to sorafenib on overall survival (HR 0.92), the direction the filed PLC/PRF/5 xenograft and Eisai's HCC panel predicted. Retrodiction ruling: efficacy is a claim about the target, and sorafenib, a VEGFR multikinase inhibitor, had already prolonged survival in HCC patients (SHARP, 2007-2008) before this model result was public, so it is scored retro. Design: non-inferiority versus sorafenib on overall survival as the primary endpoint, met; superiority not shown, while the model had shown lenvatinib at least as active as sorafenib.
efficacy.quote: Median survival time for lenvatinib of 13·6 months (95% CI 12·1-14·9) was non-inferior to sorafenib (12·3 months, 10·4-13·9; hazard ratio 0·92, 95% CI 0·79-1·06), meeting criteria for non-inferiority.
efficacy.reason: Both phase 3s matched the HCC mouse models
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: model side is Matsuki 2018 (tier 1), whose PLC/PRF/5 arm is the study Eisai filed in 2015, so the prediction preceded the trial even though its publication (May 2018) followed it; I did not add a separate retro entry for Matsuki to avoid counting one paper twice. Direction only: the model showed activity and sorafenib-comparable or better growth inhibition, the trial met non-inferiority and not superiority. Donafenib (ZGDH3, OS 12.1 vs 10.3 months) and catequentinib/anlotinib (ALTER-0802, single-arm phase 2) are listed below but score nothing: I found no preclinical HCC model paper for either (PubMed, abstract level).

patient_trials.quote: Lenvatinib was non-inferior to sorafenib in overall survival in untreated advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.

Median OS was significantly longer with donafenib than sorafenib treatment (FAS; 12.1 v 10.3 months; hazard ratio, 0.831; 95% CI, 0.699 to 0.988; P = .0245); donafenib also exhibited superior OS outcomes versus sorafenib in the intention-to-treat population.

This study aimed to assess efficacy and safety of anlotinib as a first- or second-line treatment for advanced or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma (aHCC) and to identify the predictive plasma cytokines on efficacy of anlotinib.

efficacy.note: Driver-gene screen in a multi-driver mouse HCC model: lenvatinib eliminated FGF19-expressing tumours, sorafenib MET- and NRAS-driven ones; a patient-selection prediction before any patient test.
efficacy.short: Mouse screen: FGF19 tumours are lenvatinib-sensitive
efficacy.quote: We found that lenvatinib selectively eliminated FGF19-expressing tumors, whereas sorafenib eliminated MET- and NRAS-expressing tumors.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled); the delivery method is inferred from the paper's cited methods (Sleeping Beauty transposon, hydrodynamic injection), not read in the Methods. Same-paper opening at first use.
efficacy.judgement: A distinct system from the draft's xenograft track: a genetically engineered mouse with many driver genotypes side by side, used to choose which patients respond (prediction_level patient). Matsuki 2018's Hep3B2.1-7 FGF19 xenograft belongs to the existing xenograft track and is not duplicated here.
efficacy.model: Mouse HCC with diverse genetic drivers (hydrodynamic transposon delivery) screened for lenvatinib vs sorafenib susceptibility

efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: selective elimination of FGF19-expressing tumours; patients: longer survival on lenvatinib than sorafenib in serum ST6GAL1-high (FGF19 proxy) HCC
efficacy.population: Serum ST6GAL1-high (FGF19-driven) HCC on TKI therapy
efficacy.note: Same paper: serum ST6GAL1 (an FGF19-regulated secreted protein) tracked tumour FGF19, and ST6GAL1-high patients lived longer on lenvatinib than on sorafenib.
efficacy.short: ST6GAL1-high patients do better on lenvatinib
efficacy.quote: Among patients with serum ST6GAL1-high HCC who underwent TKI therapy, lenvatinib therapy showed significantly better survival than sorafenib.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled): the patient cohort is retrospective, its size and hazard ratio were not seen, and the biomarker is a serum proxy for tumour FGF19 rather than FGF19 itself. Serum FGF19 studies point the other way (Shigesawa 2020 JGH Open: high baseline serum FGF19 plus ANG2 predicted poor lenvatinib response; Finn 2021 REFLECT: baseline serum FGF19 not predictive), but serum FGF19 is largely ileal, not tumour, so they are not scored against this track.
efficacy.judgement: Scored same at patient level: the model named the responder genotype and the same paper's patients agreed in direction. Not a retrodiction: FGF19 as a lenvatinib-selection marker was not an established clinical result before this screen. Not a trial primary endpoint (retrospective OS), so endpoint_role is null. One drug's agreement only; no prospective trial has tested it.
efficacy.model: Mouse HCC with diverse genetic drivers (hydrodynamic transposon delivery) screened for lenvatinib vs sorafenib susceptibility

efficacy.note: First member-drug use found: 52 PLC organoids from 153 patients tested on lenvatinib; resistant in vitro yet sensitive as organoid xenografts, and no patient comparison.
efficacy.short: Organoids resist lenvatinib in vitro; no patient test
efficacy.quote: PLC organoids were mostly resistant to lenvatinib in vitro but sensitive to lenvatinib in ODX models.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Earlier liver-cancer organoid papers (Broutier 2017, Nuciforo 2018) tested sorafenib only, outside the member list, so the track opens here; an earlier member-drug organoid screen may exist.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The in-vitro/in-vivo split is itself a warning that a dish cannot read an anti-angiogenic drug; recorded as untested, not contra, because no patient was compared.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary liver cancer organoids / organoid biobanks (ex vivo drug sensitivity)

efficacy.note: 399-organoid biobank (144 patients) screened on seven drugs incl. lenvatinib; abstract claims agreement with patient response, but which drug was compared could not be read.
efficacy.short: Biobank claims patient-response match; drug unread
efficacy.quote: we establish a PLC biobank, consisting of 399 tumor organoids derived from 144 patients, which recapitulates histopathology and genomic landscape of parental tumors, and is reliable for drug sensitivity screening, as evidenced by both in vivo models and patient response.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled; full text not retrievable (Cell Press blocked two scrape attempts, no PMC copy). The abstract does not name the drug(s) in the patient-response comparison, so under the no-widening rule no status is assigned until a member drug (lenvatinib is among the seven) is confirmed. LICOB (Ji 2023, doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.adg3358, PMC10949980 full text) validated lenvatinib combinations in organoids and PDX only, not against patients.
efficacy.judgement: Kept untested with strengthens: the comparison exists in the source but cannot be attributed to a class member from what I could read; a checker with the full text can turn this into same or contra for lenvatinib.
efficacy.reason: Patient comparison claimed; member drug unverified
efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary liver cancer organoids / organoid biobanks (ex vivo drug sensitivity)

safety.confidence_note: Proxy opening date: the earliest dated use of the class's toxicology species that the sources give.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus dog or monkey
safety.note: Lenvatinib's 4-week rat study was first reviewed under the IND in 2005; no patient comparison existed yet.
safety.quote: This GLP-compliant repeat-dose toxicology study in Sprague Dawley rats was originally reviewed by Wei Chen, Ph.D. in April, 2005 following submission of IND
safety.judgement: One safety track pools the standard rodent plus non-rodent GLP toxicology for the class (rat and dog for regorafenib, rat and monkey for lenvatinib); the species differ but the system and its rules are the same.

safety.magnitude_basis: liver enzyme elevation, animals vs patients
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus dog or monkey
safety.note: Rat and dog liver histopathology with enzyme rises predicted regorafenib hepatotoxicity, seen clinically and boxed on the label. Imported-harm ruling: no HCC patient safety data for this drug existed at this date, so the import stands here; HCC patients measured later (RESORCE 2016) set the status in the entry appended at the end of the cell.
safety.short: Animal liver injury matched boxed hepatotoxicity
safety.quote: Hematological changes including neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and lymphopenia as well as elevations in liver enzymes were seen clinically and hepatotoxicity is included in a black box warning for Stivarga.
safety.judgement: Comparison stated by the reviewer. Imported from the colorectal NDA population; the same hepatotoxicity later appeared in RESORCE HCC patients. On-target VEGF harms (hypertension) are also predicted in the review but the liver finding is the one the reviewer pairs with the clinic.

safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus dog or monkey
safety.note: Rat and monkey hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST rises, hepatocellular necrosis) matched the hepatotoxicity seen in lenvatinib-treated patients. Imported-harm ruling: no HCC patient safety data for this drug existed at this date, so the import stands here; HCC patients measured later (REFLECT 2018) set the status in the entry appended at the end of the cell.
safety.short: Rat and monkey liver injury matched clinic
safety.quote: Consistent with the hepatotoxicity observed in patients given lenvatinib in the clinic, hepatotoxicity was evident in rats and monkeys following lenvatinib administration.
safety.judgement: Comparison stated by the reviewer; imported from the thyroid-cancer NDA population. Hepatotoxicity was again the leading serious harm in REFLECT HCC patients, so the import holds in this disease.

safety.magnitude_basis: incidence of liver laboratory abnormalities and fatal hepatic failure versus placebo
safety.population: Unselected HCC, Child-Pugh A, progressed on sorafenib (RESORCE)
safety.confidence_note: Paired by me: model side the 2012 rat/dog findings in the regorafenib pharmacology review. Laboratory figures from label Table 6; dated to the RESORCE Lancet online publication (2016-12-06), which first reported the adverse events.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus dog or monkey
safety.note: In HCC patients (RESORCE) any-grade AST, ALT and bilirubin rises were more frequent than on placebo (93 vs 84%, 70 vs 59%, 78 vs 55%), but grade 3-4 rises and fatal hepatic failure were not; the predicted liver harm held only in mild form. Imported-harm ruling: HCC patients' own result sets the status.
safety.short: RESORCE: mild liver rises only, partial match
safety.quote: In the RESORCE study, there was no increase in the incidence of fatal hepatic failure as compared to placebo
safety.judgement: Partial rather than contra: the species predicted liver enzyme rises with histopathology and HCC patients showed excess any-grade enzyme and bilirubin rises, but not the severe or fatal hepatotoxicity seen in colorectal patients.
safety.reason: HCC patients: mild liver signal only

safety.magnitude_basis: incidence of hepatic encephalopathy and hepatic failure versus sorafenib
safety.population: Unselected HCC, first line, Child-Pugh A (REFLECT)
safety.confidence_note: Paired by me: model side the 2015 lenvatinib pharmacology review (rat and monkey hepatotoxicity). Dated to the REFLECT Lancet online publication (February 2018); the label carrying the figures is August 2018.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus dog or monkey
safety.note: In HCC patients (REFLECT) lenvatinib caused hepatic encephalopathy (8% vs 3% on sorafenib) and grade 3-5 hepatic failure (3%, as on sorafenib), the liver harm the rat and monkey studies predicted. Imported-harm ruling: HCC patients' own result sets the status.
safety.short: REFLECT: liver harm in HCC patients
safety.quote: In REFLECT (HCC), hepatic encephalopathy (including hepatic encephalopathy, encephalopathy, metabolic encephalopathy, and hepatic coma) occurred in 8% of LENVIMA-treated patients and 3% of sorafenib-treated patients.
safety.reason: Liver harm held in HCC patients
safety.judgement: Same: the harm the species predicted appeared in this disease's patients; the active comparator is itself hepatotoxic, so hepatic failure was not in excess of sorafenib but was present.
